Drift-restricted random-walk maxima and two standard invariance/CLT arguments prove the specified fixed-p limits. Separate source-level independent direct-state and bitwise checkers replay all states n≤15 and n≤20, and the Python checker verifies weighted counts at three Bernoulli odds. Their finite checks support but do not substitute for the proof.

value.rationale: The last evacuation time is a natural complete transient invariant for finite absorbing traffic. The result calculates every Bernoulli finite-time shell exactly for all path lengths and identifies a universal early shell independent of path length, plus a sharp phase transition in clearance fluctuations: tight centered law at low density, half-normal diffusive at the critical density, and Gaussian about a ballistic center above it. This is a substantive all-n classification and asymptotic analysis, not a routine assertion of convergence or a known table recomputation.
